landmarks.name: Plaza Independencia
landmarks.writeup: The main square in Montevideo, featuring the statue of national hero José Artigas and surrounded by historic buildings.

landmarks.name: Casapueblo
landmarks.writeup: A building near Punta del Este designed by artist Carlos Páez Vilaró, serving as a museum, art gallery, and hotel.

landmarks.name: Colonia del Sacramento
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its well-preserved colonial architecture and cobblestone streets.

landmarks.name: Palacio Salvo
landmarks.writeup: An iconic skyscraper in Montevideo that was once the tallest building in South America.

landmarks.name: Punta del Este Lighthouse
landmarks.writeup: A historic lighthouse offering panoramic views of the Atlantic coast and the city.

cultural_events.name: Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: A vibrant celebration featuring parades, music, and traditional candombe drumming lasting over 40 days.

cultural_events.name: Semana Criolla
cultural_events.writeup: A festival celebrating rural traditions, including rodeos, folk music, and traditional food.

cultural_events.name: Festival Internacional de Jazz de Punta del Este
cultural_events.writeup: An annual jazz festival attracting international and local musicians.

food_writeup: Uruguayan cuisine is known for its beef, especially asado (barbecue), chivito (a steak sandwich), and mate, a traditional herbal tea widely consumed.
brief_history: Uruguay gained independence in 1828 after conflicts involving Spain, Portugal, Brazil, and Argentina. It developed as a democratic nation with a strong welfare state and progressive social policies.

important_people.name: José Artigas
important_people.description: National hero and leader of the independence movement

current_conflicts: Uruguay is currently peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts.
